title: Add offline bundle import for air-gapped upgrades (manifest + signature verification)
author: Devon Price
description:
Summary: Adds an offline bundle import flow to support air-gapped / on-prem Redwood Private upgrades. The installer can now ingest an "upgrade bundle" (tar.gz) containing a manifest + artifacts, verify integrity (sha256) and authenticity (signature), then stage the artifacts into the local cache for subsequent upgrade steps. This PR also adds operator-friendly error output for invalid bundles (missing files, checksum mismatch, unsupported manifest schema version, or signature verification failure) with remediation hints and non-zero exit codes suitable for automation.

Context: Air-gapped customers cannot pull images/charts during an upgrade. We need a deterministic, verifiable bundle format that can be transported via secure channels and imported offline with strong guardrails.

What’s included: 1) New CLI: `redwood-private-installer bundle import --path <bundle.tar.gz> [--cache-dir <dir>] [--allow-unsigned (dev only)]` 2) Manifest parsing + validation: supports `manifestVersion: 1`, strict schema checks, and explicit errors for unknown fields/versions. 3) Signature verification: verifies `bundle.sig` over `manifest.json` + referenced payload digests. Uses the installer’s trusted public key set (configurable via `--trust-store` for on-prem packaging) and fails closed by default. 4) Integrity verification: computes sha256 for each artifact in the bundle (charts, image tarballs, config templates) and compares to the manifest. 5) Staging + caching: writes verified artifacts into the installer cache with a content-addressed layout; emits a stable "bundle id" (sha256 of manifest) for later diagnostics. 6) UX improvements: consistent error messages, colored output when TTY, and `--no-color` for logs; errors include the exact file, expected vs actual digest, and next-step guidance.

Out of scope: Actually running the upgrade from the offline cache (wired up in subsequent PRs) and generating bundles (handled by Release Eng tooling).

Operator usage: - Import bundle: `redwood-private-installer bundle import --path ./redwood-private-upgrade-2025.01.0.tar.gz` - Validate only (no staging): `redwood-private-installer bundle import --path ./bundle.tar.gz --dry-run` - Use a custom trust store (on-prem): `redwood-private-installer bundle import --path ./bundle.tar.gz --trust-store /etc/redwood/trust/pubkeys/`

Implementation notes: - Bundle format: tar.gz containing `manifest.json`, `bundle.sig`, and an `artifacts/` directory. - Manifest fields: `manifestVersion`, `createdAt`, `release`, `artifacts[]` (each with `name`, `type`, `path`, `sha256`, optional `sizeBytes`). - Verification order is: unpack to temp dir -> parse/validate manifest -> verify signature -> verify digests -> stage artifacts -> write import receipt (`import-receipt.json`) to cache.

Error handling: - Exit code 2: bundle format/manifest validation error - Exit code 3: signature verification failure - Exit code 4: checksum mismatch / missing artifact - Exit code 5: filesystem/write error staging to cache

Testing: - Unit tests for manifest parsing (invalid schema, unknown version, missing required fields). - Unit tests for signature verify path (valid sig, invalid sig, missing key). - Integration-ish test using a generated fixture bundle with a known checksum mismatch to validate error formatting.

Security: - Default behavior is "fail closed" (unsigned bundles are rejected). - `--allow-unsigned` is gated behind `REDWOOD_INSTALLER_ALLOW_UNSAFE=1` and prints a prominent warning. - Logging avoids printing full manifest content when signature verification fails; only prints the failing key id and reason.

Follow-ups: - Wire offline cache into `upgrade plan` and `upgrade apply` so image/chart pulls can be satisfied from staged artifacts. - Extend manifest to include OCI image index metadata (multi-arch), but keep v1 minimal for beta.

Docs: Added CLI help text + a short section in the installer README on air-gapped import expectations.

Changelog: Not user-visible for hosted users; Private on-prem customers get a new supported workflow for importing signed offline upgrade bundles.

bundle: implement tarball unpack + staging directory lifecycle
manifest: add v1 schema, strict parsing, and validation errors
security: implement signature verification against trust store
integrity: add sha256 verification for referenced artifacts
ux: standardize errors, add exit codes, and remediation hints
tests: add fixtures and unit coverage for invalid bundle cases
docs: update README and `--help` text for air-gapped bundle import
review_conversation: 2025-01-15 Connor O'Brien: Can we guarantee import is fully offline? I want to avoid any surprise network calls (e.g., key fetching).

2025-01-15 Devon Price (author): Yes. `bundle import` does not hit the network. Trust store is local-only; if no keys match we fail with a message pointing to `--trust-store`. Added a regression test that runs with `HTTP_PROXY` set and asserts no outbound calls (best-effort).
2025-01-15 Marcus Lin: Please ensure the unsigned-bundle escape hatch is clearly labeled and not accidentally used in prod. Also: don't log full signature material on failure.

2025-01-16 Devon Price (author): Updated: `--allow-unsigned` now requires `REDWOOD_INSTALLER_ALLOW_UNSAFE=1`, prints a multi-line warning, and sets a metric tag `bundle_unsigned=true` in the import receipt. Signature failure logging now prints only key id + reason.

2025-01-16 Hanae Suzuki: What exact bytes are we signing? We need a stable canonicalization to avoid "works on my machine" signature issues. Suggest signing the manifest bytes as written and verifying digests for payloads separately.

2025-01-16 Devon Price (author): Implemented as suggested: we sign the exact `manifest.json` bytes in the tarball (no re-serialization). Verification reads the raw file bytes. Payload integrity is enforced via sha256 entries in the manifest.
2025-01-17 Kenji Nakamura: Error UX looks good, but can we make the checksum mismatch output include the artifact name and path in one line for support copy/paste?
2025-01-17 Devon Price (author): Done. Checksum mismatch message now includes `artifact=<name> path=<path> expected=<sha> got=<sha>`. Also added `--no-color` support for clean copy/paste in tickets.
2025-01-17 Rafael Mendes: Add a note in help text about where the cache is written and that it can be collected in diagnostics.

2025-01-18 Devon Price (author): Added to CLI help + README. Cache defaults to `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/redwood-private-installer` or `~/.cache/...`. Import writes `import-receipt.json` which will be included in the diagnostics bundle in PR #444.
2025-01-18 Connor O'Brien: Approved. This unblocks ENG-2319; please follow up with wiring this into upgrade apply.
2025-01-18 Marcus Lin: Approved after changes. Thanks for failing closed by default.
release_notes: Private installer: Added `bundle import` command for importing signed offline upgrade bundles in air-gapped environments.
Security: Offline bundle imports now verify signature and artifact checksums by default; unsigned bundles are rejected unless explicitly allowed with an unsafe override.
